findings.element: theDayRecord() / isTheDay() — render-b.js:163-172; consumed by row()'s data-anchor (:180), setTitle() (:871) and editor()'s theDay (:916)
findings.problem: The single object the whole composition is measured from is identified by scanning F.milestones for the FIRST record whose date equals F.project.primaryDate.date — a date match alone, which the function's own comment says it never does ('never by a date match alone, which any second moment on the day would also satisfy'). The project record carries no id, so the date scan is the only path and array order decides which moment becomes the wedding. Two gestures the product explicitly supports break it. Driven at 390x844 and 1440x960, v=paper AND v=ink, from state=owner-flight: open 'Send the invitations', type '3 October 2026' — accepted, with the product's own bespoke note 'This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself.' — then rename it 'Post the invitations', Done, Preview, Back. Result, identical on both grounds: the guest's phone header reads '79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Post the invitations'. That .b-sub string is the one the unfurl card and the printed sheet also read, so the wedding is named after an errand everywhere it is sent. data-anchor — the mark that makes the day the day on the measure — has moved to 'Post the invitations', and 'Wedding day' is now an ordinary row. Opening 'Wedding day' gives aria-label 'Editing Wedding day' with 'Delete this moment' and Shown/Hidden present; baseline on the untouched fixture is 'Editing the day itself', no delete, no visibility. I pressed it: the wedding day is gone from its own plan and the horizon still counts 79 days to 'Post the invitations'. Multi-moment days are neither exotic nor unanticipated — states.day carries a plural branch ('Happening today' when todayItems.length > 1) written for exactly this case, and commitDate has a bespoke sentence for landing exactly on the day. The behaviour gate has six assertions guarding this precise property — interaction-check.mjs:2971-2975 ('exactly one row is the day', 'the day cannot be hidden from guests', 'the day cannot be deleted as a moment', 'the day's editor says what it is'), :2994 ('renaming the day renames it everywhere') and :352 ('exactly one item is the day itself') — and every one runs on the untouched fixture, where nothing else sits on 3 October. Six passing assertions proving nothing about the state one legal move away.
findings.fix: Resolve the day by id, never by date. (1) fixture.js: give the project the id it already has — project.primaryDate becomes { label: 'Wedding day', date: '2026-10-03', id: 'demo-audience-item-wedding' }. (2) render-b.js:163, theDayRecord() becomes: function theDayRecord() { var pinned = F.project.primaryDate.id && recordFor(F.project.primaryDate.id); if (pinned && pinned.date === F.project.primaryDate.date) return pinned; for (var i = 0; i < F.milestones.length; i++) { if (F.milestones[i].date === F.project.primaryDate.date) { F.project.primaryDate.id = F.milestones[i].id; return F.milestones[i]; } } return null; } — the date scan survives only as the one-time seeder for a project whose day has no milestone yet (states['owner-empty'] mints primaryDate with id: null and the synthesised day row at :241 still renders), and it stamps the id the first time it runs, so a later arrival can never take it. (3) Write the gate assertion first and watch it fail: from owner-flight move a spare moment onto the day, remount, then assert document.querySelectorAll('.b-item[data-anchor]') is exactly the wedding id; that its editor reads aria-label 'Editing the day itself' with no [data-act="delete"] and no .b-seg; that the moved row's editor reads 'Editing <its own name>' WITH both; and that renaming the moved row leaves F.project.primaryDate.label unchanged at 'Wedding day'. Run it on both grounds.

findings.element: .b-undoText, built by briefly() — render-b.js:59-62; used at :954, :982, :1137 and :1305
findings.problem: briefly() is round 11's own fix for the four-line undo bar, and it trims by character count: name.slice(0, 43).replace(/[s,;:]+$/, '') + ellipsis. Two defects in one line. (a) It cuts mid-word, the first entry under Typography in the paid-for defect library ('Trim to the last whole word, keep the full string in the accessible name and tooltip'). Ordinary wedding titles run 45-52 characters and all of them break: 'Photographs with both families by the lakeside steps' announces as 'Photographs with both families by the lake… was removed.'; 'Hair and make-up for the bridesmaids at the hotel' becomes 'Hair and make-up for the bridesmaids at the…', a complete-looking phrase with the place missing. Measured at 1440x960 and 390x844 on v=paper and v=ink, identical on all four. (b) The trailing-trim character class is /[s,;:]+$/ — it holds the LETTER s, plainly meant as backslash-s. It never strips the whitespace it was written for, and it silently eats a trailing 's': the lakeside case slices to '…by the lakes' and the regex deletes that s. The bar is role="status", so the truncated string is what a screen reader hears, and after a delete it is the ONLY remaining statement of what was removed, because the row has left the screen. .b-undoText carries no data-clamp, no data-full, no title and no visually-hidden twin — I read every attribute on it at both widths on both grounds. That is why the gate's two standing trim assertions — interaction-check.mjs:432 'every trim ends on a whole word' and :439 'a trimmed string keeps its whole self in the accessibility tree' — pass: both iterate document.querySelectorAll('[data-clamp]'), which on owner-flight is exactly the seven row titles and never the one string the product truncates in JavaScript. The gate's own long-title test at :3296 uses a 99-character title and asserts only /moved 7 days later/; it never reads the half of the sentence that names the moment.
findings.fix: render-b.js:59 — function briefly(record) { var name = nameOf(record); if (name.length <= 44) return name; var cut = name.slice(0, 43); var space = cut.lastIndexOf(' '); if (space >= 20) cut = cut.slice(0, space); return cut.replace(/[\s,;:]+$/, '') + '\u2026'; }. The result is never longer than today's, so the 64px band and the label's 22-24px of air are unaffected. Then bring the string inside the gate that already exists for it: in paintUndo(), when the leading part differs from nameOf(top.record), wrap the name in a span carrying data-clamp, data-full set to the whole title and aria-hidden="true", followed by the sibling span[data-clamp-full="true"] holding the full title in the visually-hidden class — the exact shape .b-title already uses, so interaction-check.mjs:432 and :439 start covering it with no new assertion written. Confirm they fail against the current code first.

findings.element: the [data-act="owner"] return from Preview — render-b.js go() / wireOwner
findings.problem: The owner's most repeated loop is: find a row, change it, check what the guest sees, come back, next row. The return leg throws the plan back to the top every time. Driven on owner-flight scrolled to the foot of the measure, press Preview, press Back to the plan: at 390x844 scrollY goes 1184 -> 0 (the entire plan), at 768x1024 1483 -> 0, at 1279x800 and 1280x900 107 -> 0; focus lands on H1.b-who. Identical on v=ink. Going to the top ON the preview is right — it is a different surface. Coming back is not: the owner is returned to a screen they were already standing in, a full measure away from the row they were working on. This is the first entry under Interaction in the paid-for defect library, and the product already implements the remedy for its own undo (remember() captures entry.at and entry.paneAt and undo() restores both in a finally block) — the machinery exists and this one transition does not use it. The gate does not cover it: :1414-1421 asserts only that the plan is not destroyed (item count) and :1487 that preview 'lands on something' (activeElement !== body) and 'says where it went' (live region non-empty). Nothing reads a scroll offset across the round trip.
findings.fix: In wireOwner's click handler, on [data-act="preview"], capture before go('desk'): var pane0 = paneOf(root); cameFromOwner = { y: window.scrollY, pane: pane0 ? pane0.scrollTop : null }; — hang it on the module-level flag that already survives the transition, not on the root that is about to be discarded. On [data-act="owner"], after go('owner-flight') and inside the requestAnimationFrame that already restores focus, replay it: if (place) { window.scrollTo(0, place.y); var back = paneOf(document.querySelector('.b-field')); if (back && typeof place.pane === 'number') back.scrollTop = place.pane; }, and pass preventScroll on the focus call so the restore is not immediately undone. Gate assertion, written first and failing: at 390 and 768, scroll owner-flight to its foot, Preview, Back, assert Math.abs(scrollY - before) <= 2 on both grounds.

findings.problem: The one screen the whole company is judged by sorts the day's own moments with a.title.localeCompare(b.title). Driven at 390 and 1440 on both grounds with four moments dated 3 October, the wedding morning prints, in this order under 'Happening today': Ceremony at St John's / Dinner and speeches / Drinks in the walled garden / Wedding day. Dinner before drinks. A stacked list read top to bottom is a sequence, and this one is a false sequence — alphabetical order handed to a venue and a celebrant at 8am as the running order of the day. Nothing else in the product orders anything by name; every other list is ordered by distance, and where distance ties the fallback should be the arrangement a person made, not the dictionary. Second defect in the same three lines: the block prints m.title raw rather than nameOf(m), the single naming accessor whose own comment at :41 says it is 'used by the row, the accessible name, every receipt and the editor'. states.day is the one surface that skips it, so a moment the owner never named renders as an empty paragraph — measured height 0 — while the row on every other screen reads 'Untitled moment' and every count still includes it. A shown moment silently absent from the morning is the silent-content-deletion class. Neither case is hypothetical: the plural branch ('Happening today' when todayItems.length > 1) was written for a day carrying several moments.
findings.fix: render-b.js:2006-2008 — drop the sort and keep the record's own order, which is the order the owner arranged: var todayItems = F.live().filter(function (m) { return m.date && daysFrom(clock, m.date) === 0; });. At :2024 route the name through the accessor: h('p.b-dayNowTitle', { 'data-type': 'title', text: nameOf(m) }). Gate assertion, written first and failing: seed three moments on the primary date in a deliberately non-alphabetical record order plus one with title '', render state=day, and assert the .b-dayNowTitle strings come back in record order and that none of them is empty, on both grounds.

biggestWin: The new owner's first two minutes are now genuinely finished, and they are the hardest thing on this surface to get right. The empty project asks one question, states the format in a line that survives typing rather than a placeholder that vanishes at the first keystroke, and answers three wrong inputs with three different true sentences — empty, unreadable, and gone — instead of the one string that used to tell a person who typed nothing that what they typed was not a date. When the day is accepted the screen stops asking the question: the heading, the field and the button are replaced by the count, the ceremonial date, the today rule and one instruction. Add a moment then lands on owner-flight with the editor already open and the cursor in the title field, on a plan that is genuinely theirs — draft, unpublished, stamped today, with no invented label standing in for a name nobody has written. Driven end to end at 390 and 1440 on both grounds it never once contradicts itself, and the loading frame it would have arrived through sets its today rule within 0.3px of where the real header puts it. That is comprehension without training, which is the whole test.
